transcript:
This message comes from Synchrony Bank, who wants to inspire you to stay flexible, save
smart and keep dreaming big.
With their high-yield savings account, you'll earn a great rate without monthly fees or
minimums so you can reach your savings goals faster without the hassle.
Open an account with a great rate in five minutes or less and dream on.
Go to Synchrony.com/NPR, Member FDIC.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Dave Mattingly.
With more than half the votes counted in Israel's election, there's still no clear winner.
Neither Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu nor his main challenger have secured a majority
needed to form a government.
NPR's Ruth Sherlock is in Tel Aviv.
Arab-led parties had a historical showing in this election.
They represent about 20 percent of the population here in Israel, but they don't usually vote
in such large numbers.
In the town of Abu Ghosh near Jerusalem, which has a majority of Palestinian citizens in
Israel, I asked restaurant owner Baha Abdul Rahman what was different this time.
He said Palestinians with Israeli citizenship wanted to change what he calls a vengeful
government because they've been demonized and discriminated against since the October
7 attacks by Hamas in Israel three years ago.
That's NPR's Ruth Sherlock in Tel Aviv.
A federal judge in California is denying a request by the Justice Department to set aside
thousands of ballots sent out by the state for the November midterm elections.
The DOJ is appealing that ruling, as NPR's Jew Joffee Block reports.
The Justice Department wants to stop California election officials from processing ballots
pertaining to 20,000 individuals that federal officials say are likely non-citizens.
California officials argued the DOJ's list is unreliable and said the demand to set aside
the ballots is infeasible.
Judge David Carter rejected the DOJ's request, expressing concern about disenfranchising voters
and potential election chaos.
He wrote if the executive branch can "discount votes and threaten an ongoing election due
to unproven allegations, then our democracy is in danger."
Jew Joffee Block, NPR News.
Calls for a no-confidence vote have been mounting at Cornell after a former student, known as
Jane Doe, claimed she was gang-raped at a fraternity house in 2024.
While some faculty attempted to delay the vote against Cornell's president, that effort
failed during a heated and divisive meeting on Wednesday.
Mike Thompson, a professor at the university, called the no-confidence resolution "meaningless."
Thompson and other suggested faculty wait until an independent investigation provides
new information.
But proponents of the measure say it signals solidarity with sexual assault survivors.
Faculty at Cornell will have one week to vote on the resolution.
For NPR News, I'm Jung Yun Han in Ithaca.
This is NPR News from Washington.
Alaska's Democratic Senate candidate, Mary Peltola, is dismissing a report in The New
York Times that alleges her campaign was involved in efforts to recruit a candidate to her race
with the same name as incumbent Republican Senator Dan Sullivan.
That candidate is retired schoolteacher Dan J. Sullivan, who's also on the ballot.
The Times cites text messages between members of Peltola's campaign, discussing the recruitment
of a candidate with the same name as the two-term GOP Senator.
Peltola calls the report a distraction.
Dan J. Sullivan has denied having contact with Peltola's campaign.
The Milwaukee Brewers are World Series champions after beating the Tampa Bay Rays in Game 5
last night 4-1.
Sean Kenan with member station WMNF was at Tropicana Field as the Brewers finished off
the Rays in Major League Baseball's Fall Classic.
The Brewers hoisted their first World Series trophy in franchise history on the Rays' home
field.
Brewers fan Travis Ryland is from near Green Bay and celebrated after watching the final
out from the right field stands of Tropicana Field.
I'm speechless.
Speechless.
I've been new in all these playoffs since 2008 and I'm speechless.
I'm in tears right now.
Brewers starting pitcher Jacob Mizorowski went nearly six innings, throwing 100 mile an hour
fastballs and giving up no runs.
The Rays made a push in the bottom of the ninth, but only managed a single run.
For NPR News, I'm Sean Kenan at the World Series in St. Petersburg, Florida.
I'm Dave Mattingly, NPR News, in Washington.

topics.text: Israel's election has no clear winner as Arab-led parties post historic turnout
Federal judge rejects Justice Department request to set aside thousands of California ballots
Cornell faculty face one-week vote on no-confidence resolution over Jane Doe assault claim
Alaska Senate candidate Mary Peltola dismisses New York Times report on same-name candidate recruitment
Milwaukee Brewers beat Tampa Bay Rays 4-1 in Game 5 to win World Series
